title: finding(permissions): `evaluateCondition`'s prototype-name guard closes three spellings, not the class — `{ field: 'toString', operator: 'neq' }` still admits every record
body:
Measured while implementing objectui#7751, which brings `DataScopeManager` up to this evaluator's hardening standard. The sibling was the control, and the control has the same defect it was being used to fix — one layer over.

## The measurement

`packages/permissions/src/evaluator.ts` refuses three field names by list and reads the rest with `hasOwnProperty`:

```
if (['__proto__', 'constructor', 'prototype'].includes(condition.field)) return false;
const value = Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(record, condition.field) ? record[condition.field] : undefined;
```

`hasOwnProperty` collapses **inherited** into **absent**, and on a negative operator absent ADMITS. So every prototype member that is *not* one of the three named spellings still admits every record. Probed against head source, record `{ id: 1, tenant: 'acme' }`:

| `condition.field` | `neq` | `not_in` | `eq` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `__proto__` | false | false | false |
| `constructor` | false | false | false |
| `prototype` | false | false | false |
| `toString` | **true** | **true** | false |
| `valueOf` | **true** | **true** | false |
| `hasOwnProperty` | **true** | **true** | false |
| `isPrototypeOf` | **true** | **true** | false |

`true` on a row-level condition means the record passes the rule that exists to hide it. Same failure direction as objectui#7378 and objectui#7751 — admit, silently — on the same permission boundary. The name list cannot close this: it enumerates spellings, and `Object.prototype` has more of them than any list will hold.

## Second measurement, same read

`hasOwnProperty` also **widens** for records whose field value is inherited (an `Object.create` parent, a class instance with an accessor on the prototype). Record `Object.create({ tenant: 'acme' })`:

- `{ field: 'tenant', operator: 'neq', value: 'acme' }` returns **true** — the record's tenant IS `acme`, and the rule that hides `acme` rows admits it.
- `{ field: 'tenant', operator: 'not_in', value: ['acme'] }` returns **true**, likewise.

## The shape that closes it

objectui#7751 landed this in `DataScopeManager` and it is available to copy. Read the field in three cases rather than two, so that *inherited* and *genuinely absent* stop being the same answer:

1. name in the refused list, or
2. an own member — its value, or
3. not own: if the name resolves on the prototype chain at all (`field in Object(record)`) the read is REFUSED and the rule denies; if it does not resolve, the field is genuinely absent and `undefined` is returned, so ordinary "this record has no `status`" rules keep the verdicts they have today.

Case 3 is the whole fix. Measured on `DataScopeManager` over a 2772-case matrix, adopting it narrowed 352 verdicts and widened **zero** — including zero change to genuinely-absent-field verdicts, which is the regression this shape is most likely to cause and does not.

## Why this is filed rather than fixed

objectui#7751's dispatch scopes `packages/permissions` as read-only reference; its fix lands in `packages/core` only. Filing rather than folding in, so the change to a second permission boundary gets its own review.

Prior art for the class: objectui#4442 (`rowHeight: 'toString'` returning a function from an unguarded key index).

Refs: objectui#7751 · objectui#7378 · `packages/permissions/src/evaluator.ts` lines 128-134.
